blocks.text: Agent SDK 让你能够快速构建和部署按照你团队方式工作的智能体。它们响应你团队已经在处理的事件，并遵循你团队可以检查和更改的策略。

inlines.text: Agent SDK 让你能够快速构建和部署按照你团队方式工作的智能体。它们响应你团队已经在处理的事件，并遵循你团队可以检查和更改的策略。

blocks.text: 代码审查就是一个例子。每个团队对于什么需要关注以及谁应该审查都有自己的标准。借助 Agent SDK，你可以构建一个响应来自 GitHub、GitLab 或 Bitbucket 的拉取请求事件的智能体。该智能体可以评估变更的风险，将其路由到正确的团队，并批准符合你策略的变更。

inlines.text: 代码审查就是一个例子。每个团队对于什么需要关注以及谁应该审查都有自己的标准。借助 Agent SDK，你可以构建一个响应来自 GitHub、GitLab 或 Bitbucket 的拉取请求事件的智能体。该智能体可以评估变更的风险，将其路由到正确的团队，并批准符合你策略的变更。

blocks.text: 举个例子，Cursor 内部的一个团队构建了一个庞大且快速增长的经验教训知识库，并希望每个拉取请求都对照它进行检查。这样，即使代码库发生变化，团队过去的决策也能保持有效。借助 Agent SDK，他们在大约一天内构建了 kb-reviewer。它现在运行在他们主代码库的每个 PR 上，标记与已记录经验相矛盾的变更，引用每个发现背后的笔记，并鼓励工程师协调它所报告的差异。

blocks.text: Software teams use agents defined as code to handle recurring work across the development lifecycle. These agents connect to the places where a team works and act when relevant events occur, whether that means reviewing a pull request, executing a compliance workflow, or investigating an incident.

inlines.text: Software teams use agents defined as code to handle recurring work across the development lifecycle. These agents connect to the places where a team works and act when relevant events occur, whether that means reviewing a pull request, executing a compliance workflow, or investigating an incident.

blocks.text: The most useful agents are tailored to how a particular team operates. Until now, building one has generally meant adopting a product designed around someone else's workflow or starting from scratch.

inlines.text: The most useful agents are tailored to how a particular team operates. Until now, building one has generally meant adopting a product designed around someone else's workflow or starting from scratch.

blocks.text: Today, we're releasing the Agent SDK, the framework we use to build our own managed agents like Bugbot, Security Reviewer, and Rollouts. Agent SDK allows you to define agents in code and manage them like any other software project. Start from a template or point your coding agent at our docs. When the agent is ready, agent-sdk deploy it to Cursor infrastructure with one command.

blocks.text: Build around your workflow

inlines.text: Build around your workflow

blocks.text: The Agent SDK lets you quickly build and deploy agents that work the way your team does. They respond to the events your team already handles and follow policies your team can inspect and change.

inlines.text: The Agent SDK lets you quickly build and deploy agents that work the way your team does. They respond to the events your team already handles and follow policies your team can inspect and change.

blocks.text: Code review is one example. Each team has its own standards for what requires attention and who should review it. With the Agent SDK, you can build an agent that responds to pull request events from GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket. The agent can assess the risk of a change, route it to the right team, and approve changes that meet your policy.

inlines.text: Code review is one example. Each team has its own standards for what requires attention and who should review it. With the Agent SDK, you can build an agent that responds to pull request events from GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket. The agent can assess the risk of a change, route it to the right team, and approve changes that meet your policy.

blocks.text: As an example, a team within Cursor had built a large, fast-growing knowledge base of lessons learned and wanted every pull request checked against it. This way, the team's past decisions would hold even as the codebase changed. With the Agent SDK, they built kb-reviewer in about a day. It now runs on every PR in their main codebase, flags changes that contradict a recorded lesson, cites the note behind each finding, and encourages engineers to reconcile the discrepancies it reports.

blocks.text: For more complicated work, agents can hand a task to another specialized agent with its own tools and sessions. They can also divide a job among subagents working in parallel.

blocks.text: The Agent SDK also supports evals and event replay out of the box, allowing for rapid development with assurances that critical workflows execute the way you expect. The PGA Tour uses the Agent SDK to power their software development factory. Evals keep them moving quickly.

And built-in support for evals allows us to quickly iterate on new ideas and optimize existing capabilities reliably.

blocks.text: An Agent SDK agent is organized like a small software project. The instructions that guide it sit alongside code for its tools, connections to outside services, and the evals used to test it.

inlines.text: An Agent SDK agent is organized like a small software project. The instructions that guide it sit alongside code for its tools, connections to outside services, and the evals used to test it.

blocks.text: Each file represents something the agent knows or can do. Prompts are written in Markdown, while tools are defined as TypeScript functions. Because everything is code, changes can go through the same version control and review process as the rest of your software.

blocks.text: Deploy agents wherever you need them

inlines.text: Deploy agents wherever you need them

blocks.text: When you're ready to put an agent into use, you can deploy it to Cursor by running agent-sdk deploy from the project directory. The command builds the agent, gives it a URL, and starts it on our infrastructure. You can manage secrets and integrations from the dashboard, while continuing to use the same logs, evals, and playground available locally.

inlines.text: When you're ready to put an agent into use, you can deploy it to Cursor by running
agent-sdk deploy

from the project directory. The command builds the agent, gives it a URL, and starts it on our infrastructure. You can manage secrets and integrations from the dashboard, while continuing to use the same logs, evals, and playground available locally.

blocks.text: You can also run the agent on your own infrastructure. Each agent runs as a single Node process that can be packaged in a container.
